for_you_if: you can master steep learning curves

you are short on storage space

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Players struggle with clunky building tools and unskippable tutorials while experiencing technical crashes.

claims.claim: This cohort describes the building system, camera controls, and path placement as clunky, unintuitive, and difficult to navigate.

citations.review_text: The graphics are beautiful but oh my god this has to be THE WORST building system known to mankind. Holy Jesus. Whoever developed this clearly never built with it ONCE because OH MY GOD what IS that?? There's no building mode for the camera, there's no proper rotation settings and don't even get me started on placing walls. I made through the tutorial and immediately uninstalled because hell no. I'm sorry but please add at least a top down view for the love of god

lets take a zoo game and make it overly complicated to navigate , like I've never been so frustrated trying to build a starting zoo, I'm not even kidding you I've not even got past the tutorial, because I quit, tried to start a new zoo franchise thinking screw this ill learn as I go along . and yeah I gave up on that fairly fast , lost interest and went to play magic the gathering. utter horrible game with probably tonnes of potential. will not be playing in future and im glad i only payed 2 quid for it

These are some of the worst building controls I have ever had to try to use. Not having an option to turn on gridding snapping for all objects and no mass path painting is insane. Like, obviously some people love that kind of freedom, but it should be something you can toggle. After digging through Reddit and realizing there aren't work arounds makes this genuinely unplayable for me.

The game looks like a lot of fun, but honestly getting into it, I thought it would be more like how Jurassic World does its building, then management from there. The build mechanics are super weird and non-descriptive and there is no easy to find tutorial on how to build. So although i bought this game for two dollars, I found no satisfaction.

I wanted to like this game but the controls are so awful I can't get into it. It's a shame it looks beautiful but I want to play a game and have fun, not fight the worst user design implementation I've ever seen by a developer.

I heard someone say that this is the rite of passage to ZooTycoon 2 but I'll tell you that it is not. ZooTycoon 2 does everything this game does but better in every way. There is no brush to quickly install a bunch of appropriate scenery and you are expected to place it all yourself. You are expected to meticulously handcraft something that resembles a habitat with a really janky system that for some reason can place plants flying in the air.

The tutorial level is infuriating. I accidentally made a really hilariously small window and wanted to add more but the game was like "no, no... you made this and now accept it". I proceeded to fight the UI for 30 seconds trying to add more windows before accepting my fate and watching people just gather around the worlds tinyest window like kids around a smartphone.

good game so far. it's late here so will play more in the morning and update review once ive learned a little more but what in the good lords name is the path system? it's so unbelievably clunky.

the dialogue in the tutorials is also painfully long. still, quite fun.

The Idea of this game is brillant, but the controls and the camera is not, I have struggled to move around the map, it tells you to do certain steps but you cant move around freely to be able to follow these steps, such a shame as this could be such a good game, I wasted my money on this game.

Honestly, I was quite excited to play this. I love tycoon style games where you can still customise aspects (e.g. I love roller coaster tycoons, shop tycoons etc.), but this game felt a little too confusing to me. 
Maybe I wasn't as interested as I thought, or it might have been the fact that the tutorial levels were slow and a little too draining for me. For example, the voice of the tutorial people is unskippable/unspeedable, and so you have to listen to them speak for ages. 
It was quite cool to take care of animals in a deeper way than just feeding them and putting them in a habitat, but all the rest of the learning was super difficult. The whole staffing system was super hard to grapple at first and the work zones too. 
A lot of building is required too, so you need to put a lot of time into it.
Overall for me personally it was a 5/10, but if you're super willing to put in the work to learn everything then it would be much better for you.

claims.claim: The game suffers from performance degradation and low frame rates on powerful hardware once the zoo grows larger or when editing terrain and habitats.

citations.review_text:
The sheer volume of hours I spent on Zoo Tycoon as meant this game was a must purchase. The reality is though, this isn't Zoo Tycoon, it looks like a shiny new version of it, but it's not. 

There is a lot of freedom in this game. Same with Planet Coaster. With enough creativity and time, you can make something really special. I have neither. I wanted some creativity but there's a lot of micromanaging and less tycoony elements to this game than you'd think. These series are games for artists and there's a reason I work in an office not a studio. It's not a bad thing...it's just not for me and that makes me sad. It's a slow game too. Peacfully crafting your zoo makes the hours fly by. Shame nothing really progressed though and i found by habitat 5 or 6, I was starting to get a bit bored. You need that creative spark. Or patience. Ask my wife and she'll confirm I like both.

It is cute seeing all the animals though. I played with headphones on and found it super relaxing. The DLC can get pricey sadly and you really need a good chunk of it to make the most of the game, especially the Steam workshop.  

Played this on a a Steam Deck in Desktop Mode on a mouse and keyboard and it struggles very quickly once your zoo starts to get bigger...even on lower settings. 

Maybe with new hardware and the right mindset i'll come back to this game.

the controls are also a massive pain, especially the build mode controls. if the sims controls is like learning your multiplication tables, this is like rocket science. everything takes 100x longer than necessary to do as a result.
luckily I got it on sale, but at full price, it’s a total waste of money (and time). super disappointed.

👍 Recommended | ⭐ 9/10

"I came for the cute animals... stayed for the 200 hours of 'one last habitat.'

Planet Zoo is easily one of the best management games I've played. Every animal feels alive, and it's incredibly satisfying to watch a zoo you built from scratch become successful. The amount of customization is insane—you can spend hours perfecting a single exhibit and still have fun doing it.

The path system can test your patience, and the learning curve is steeper than I expected. But once everything clicks, it's almost impossible to put the game down.

If you enjoy city builders, simulation games, or just love animals, this is a must-play. Buy it on sale with a few DLCs, and you'll get hundreds of hours of entertainment.

Pros:
✔️ Amazing animal AI and animations
✔️ Endless creativity and customization
✔️ Relaxing yet rewarding gameplay
✔️ Great replay value

Cons:
❌ Path building can be frustrating
❌ DLC collection gets expensive

9/10 – My animals are happier than I am. Worth every minute. 🦁🐘🐼

It's hard for me to say I don't recommend this because there's lot of good stuff about the game, but there's a lot of really bad stuff. It's a decent game with some fun zoo mechanics. However, there are game design issues that impact enjoyability. First, there is no global grid, every time you place something it creates a custom grid. This means it is IMPOSSIBLE to fully match paths and buildings from different areas. Second, the paths are incredibly finicky and often create interference when placing buildings next to them. Third, the campaign is just one LONG tutorial and is manly there to teach you what bad designs look like. Fourth, the thing I really hate, the basic buildings will snap to each other, but the buildings with a fascade don't. So you have to choose to either have things all wonky or spend a ton of time decorating your store front. 

All-in-all, I only paid like $20 for the game and a handful of dlcs on sale so it was worth it, but no way would I pay full-price for this game or the dlcs.

This game is not what I had in mind. I had heard about how detailed it was so I had mentally prepared myself for it, but so much of it is very unintuitive. And sometimes it seems uneccessarily detailed. I knew when they started talking about heat maps that this wasn't right for me. There's just way too much to do, and it's a time and energy intensive game to even learn how to play. Someone else's review mentioned that they needed to watch YT tutoritals to figure things out, and I think I would have to do the same to make sense of the controls and everything in the long run.

Honestly, I never even got past the tutorital because this game has one of the worst tutorials I have ever played. Nancy won't stop yapping and everything is 'vitally important'. It is gruelling and unrelenting, which is not what you want to say for a tutorial. 

It's a pretty frustrating game, and you need to have the correct temperament for it I suppose, which I don't. And if you're a beginner, don't expect to have fun or be entertained in the beginning. For someone out there, the finnicky microdetails and micromanagement is a dream come true. But that makes this a niche experience, really not for everyone.
The game at first is honesty really fiddly cause all the controls are pretty different to other sandbox games but once you get the hang of it. its actually really fun and addictive

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the path system as difficult to use, limiting, and frustrating to align properly with enclosures.

citations.review_text: Incredible graphics, solid gameplay. It is so detailed with the features. Paths are difficult but incredibly adaptable.

I absolutely love Planet Zoo — it’s fun, intricate, and offers a huge variety of building options along with incredible animals and exhibits. The level of detail makes it both entertaining and educational, since you can actually learn about the animals while playing.

That said, the pathing system could definitely be improved, as it sometimes feels limiting. I’d also love to see more flexibility for creative, modern building layouts. From what I’ve seen, Planet Zoo 2 looks like it will address these areas, which is really exciting.

Overall, Planet Zoo is an amazing game that combines creativity, management, and education in a way that keeps me coming back for more.
very good game, can't wait for the sequel. no notes other than the usual pathing complaints :)

The GOAT of all zoo tycoons, sure it has its quirks "Paths being a pain" for example. Does not stop it from being the greatest zoo tycoon to exist. from park management too animal control and management. Looking forward to the 2nd Planet Zoo. 
I do wish they produced more free updates. 
Most of the updates are DLC related and their is a lottttt! of DLC$!

The path system is so primitive that it destroys the entire game for me.  What if I want to just place a perfect square path down to make a large standing area in my park?  Nope, can't do that.  It's just so awful it makes me want to drop kick every single plushie I see at the local city zoo I've visited.

Try aligning an enclosure perfectly with a path, or even the other way around... Nope, not without a vast amount of time and eyeballing it and prayers.

I'm sorry Frontier, what you have in PC2 should have been rushed into PZ1 at ambulatory speeds and not waited for Planet zoo 2 even if you wanted to make a DLC for it.  The path system in both PC1 and Planet Zoo  is pathetic and should have lost somebody their job for putting this into an otherwise beautiful game.

If you are thinking of buying this game, then I would suggest waiting for the second game that is coming out in October. I promise it will be worth every single dollar (I think). Anyways, this is MY personal opinion. If you don't want to wait that long, then just buy this game. Have a great day and God bless !! Isaiah 40:31 <3

You can really feel the comittment they had to make the best dang zoo game they possibly could, not just for 2019 but all the way up to 2026. I think this game is well worth its price tag. 
Even if the entrance difficulty level is a little steep, the tutorial goes a long way to helping you play the game on a base level. After that you have a HUGE community that can help you learn and explore the VAST possibilities of the modular building system, and make your own buildings, fences and habitats that blend in perfectly with your theme or the landscape around it. 

Is this game worth buying months before launch? claims.claim: Reviewers note that path placement mechanics are difficult and limited to use.

citations.review_text: Incredible graphics, solid gameplay. It is so detailed with the features. Paths are difficult but incredibly adaptable.

I absolutely love Planet Zoo — it’s fun, intricate, and offers a huge variety of building options along with incredible animals and exhibits. The level of detail makes it both entertaining and educational, since you can actually learn about the animals while playing.

That said, the pathing system could definitely be improved, as it sometimes feels limiting. I’d also love to see more flexibility for creative, modern building layouts. From what I’ve seen, Planet Zoo 2 looks like it will address these areas, which is really exciting.

Overall, Planet Zoo is an amazing game that combines creativity, management, and education in a way that keeps me coming back for more.
very good game, can't wait for the sequel. no notes other than the usual pathing complaints :)

Most of the updates are DLC related and their is a lottttt! of DLC$!

The path system is so primitive that it destroys the entire game for me.  What if I want to just place a perfect square path down to make a large standing area in my park?  Nope, can't do that.  It's just so awful it makes me want to drop kick every single plushie I see at the local city zoo I've visited.

Try aligning an enclosure perfectly with a path, or even the other way around... Nope, not without a vast amount of time and eyeballing it and prayers.

I'm sorry Frontier, what you have in PC2 should have been rushed into PZ1 at ambulatory speeds and not waited for Planet zoo 2 even if you wanted to make a DLC for it.  The path system in both PC1 and Planet Zoo  is pathetic and should have lost somebody their job for putting this into an otherwise beautiful game.
